title: Huangshan · Even Immortals Need Footpaths
summary: Bright lights can mislead, and experts can be stubborn. A cry for help leads to someone who admits his limits, then proves with firsthand signs that a good route needs more than one kind of evidence.

S01-01.title: Misty Huangshan Foothills
S01-01.summary: A voice in the mist offers heavenly guidance. Youbai rushes to meet a fellow expert. The woodcutter stops it: that's its own echo.
S01-01.objective: Confirm the way into the mountain and the mystery of the hidden stream
S01-01.result: You find the woodcutter and agree to check the paths and hidden-stream clues first.
lines: At Huangshan's foot, the abbot's copied page shows two outlets for one hidden stream. From the mist comes a drawn-out call: This... waaay...
A fellow practitioner dwells here! I shall seek their counsel.
Hold off on the networking. Doesn't that voice sound rather like you?
It is. The echo goes round the ridge and comes back a little late.
Youbai floats a few paces away, then hears its own pompous introduction. It drifts back, its flame a little smaller.
I was primarily testing the mountain's acoustic properties.
Then rest those properties. If you're checking the hidden stream, learn the path in front of you first.
Come on, elder. Your fellow expert only seems to repeat things.

S01-02.title: Rest Below the Mountain
S01-02.summary: The harder Youbai shines, the whiter the fog becomes. The woodcutter drapes a headcloth over the glare, turning divine radiance into useful light.
S01-02.objective: Ask the woodcutter how to read the trail reliably
S01-02.result: You learn to combine three signs: shoeprints, old stone steps, and the sound of water.
lines: Thick fog is no trouble. I shall shine brighter.
The blue flame flares. Everything turns whiter. You nearly mistake the woodcutter's woodpile for the mountain gate.
I can see nothing much more clearly now!
Less light. Keep it close. The path is under your feet, not in your grand entrance.
The woodcutter hangs his old headcloth on the bamboo pole to shade the glare. Cracks, shoeprints, and worn steps become visible together.
Have you... built me a canopy?
Canopies have their uses. Hear the stream to the left, find the old steps by the pine roots, and check the fresh prints. Walk when all three agree.
Bear with it, elder. You're considerably more useful like this.

S01-03.title: Paths Beneath the Pines
S01-03.summary: The glowing mist looks fit for immortals, but nobody seems to have walked there. The real steps are muddy and damp. They lead to a very real cry for help.
S01-03.objective: Choose a route using the steps, shoeprints, and stream sounds
S01-03.result: You follow the old steps on the left through the fog and hear a hunter calling for help.
lines: Three routes divide ahead. The middle has the brightest mist. The right offers a short scree slope. The left has old steps marked with muddy shoeprints.
For sheer atmosphere, the middle route is exceptional.
We're finding a path, not choosing a landscape cover shot.
You tap the right slope with your pole. A loose stone tumbles away. On the left, the stream runs close below the slope; fresh prints continue along the steps without turning back.
All three signs point left. This time, I lead with evidence.
Good. We can discuss heavenly atmosphere once we arrive.
Beyond the fog, the call becomes clear: Save me! And, if convenient, save my cakes!
Sounds real enough. Immortals rarely add that last request.
hints: Consider all three signs the woodcutter mentioned.
Only the left route has old steps, fresh shoeprints, and stream sounds close below the slope.
Choose the left route with shoeprints, old steps, and nearby running water.
options: Follow the left route: shoeprints, old steps, nearby water
All three clues agree. You pass through the fog and hear a call for help.
Follow the brightest mist in the middle
Brightness isn't a path. Youbai's silence provides a useful footnote.
Take the shortcut up the right-hand scree slope
A stone scouts the route for you by falling down it. The findings do not recommend following.

S01-04.title: Sketch the Huangshan Route
S01-04.summary: The hunter produces his own stream notes. Youbai almost mistakes a chewed hole for a second outlet. The expert is rescued; his map still needs checking.
S01-04.objective: Add the verified path and hidden-stream entrance to the sketch
S01-04.result: The mountain-route sketch is ready. You mark the hidden-stream entrance and leave the downhill course for verification.
lines: The stream bends behind that rock wall. Here, my own notes. No immortal middlemen involved.
He unfolds the notebook. A round hole sits beside the mountain outline. Youbai leans closer, eyes bright.
A second outlet! Both old maps had evidence after all.
That bit was just chewed off.
The paper has a tunnel, elder. The mountain doesn't, yet.
The notes on the back still record water sounds, damp marks, and old steps. You mark the entrance you've verified and leave the outlet blank.
Master Zhou studies the plants downhill. Master Willow knows the old names by the stream. Don't rely on me alone.
That's valuable advice. Someone who knows the way can also admit which parts they don't know.

S01-05.title: Trace the Stream
S01-05.summary: The floating leaves circle back. Youbai is about to announce uphill-flowing water when the real outlet sends them downstream. Let the evidence finish its journey.
S01-05.objective: Complete the hidden stream's course using the flow and terrain
S01-05.result: You connect the hidden stream to the lower outlet on the left and complete the Huangshan sketch.
lines: You place three broad leaves upstream. They circle in an eddy, then drift back toward you.
Look! Reversing waters! Perhaps the old map conceals a deeper mystery—
Let it finish the lap first.
The current carries the leaves down and left. One by one, all three emerge from the lower outlet. The high channel on the right stays dry, its old moss unmoved.
So that first bend was an eddy, not another river.
You will note my very precise use of 'perhaps.'
Lucky you left yourself those two syllables. Otherwise we'd need a bridge-sized patch for your dignity.
Leaves, watermarks, and elevation agree. You draw the hidden stream's connection. This time, nobody finishes their speech before the water does.
hints: Watch where the floating leaves actually emerge.
The lower-left outlet is low and wet. The right-hand channel is dry, with old moss.
Choose to connect the hidden stream to the lower outlet on the left.
options: Connect the stream to the lower-left outlet
The leaves and terrain confirm each other. The watercourse is complete.
Connect it to the higher dry channel on the right
Water has ambitions, but it hasn't signed up for climbing. Check the height and damp marks again.
Draw both outlets for a more impressive map
This is a map, not a menu. You can't order everything that looks nice. Draw only what the evidence supports.

S01-06.title: Mountain Lost in Fog
S01-06.summary: The woodcutter advises waiting out the fog. Youbai recalls a place-name nobody uses anymore. This time its memory is useful; it merely forgot to ask what people call it now.
S01-06.objective: Learn how to travel safely in thick mountain fog
S01-06.result: You record fog-weather trail advice and further details behind the mountain-path rumors.
lines: When the fog closes in, wait. Don't charge up a slope you don't know. Mountains rarely rush people. People do that themselves.
This place was called Echo Hollow. Wind turns in from the west; sound arrives from the east.
Echo Hollow? The old folk mentioned that. We call it Resting Bend now.
No wonder shouting only made things worse. That memory is useful, elder.
Youbai perks up and nearly flares again. You gently lift the shading cloth back into place.
Yes, yes. Light the feet. A little praise won't make me forget.
Keep the old name, and note today's route. Together they'll save the next traveler's knees.
Both go on the map. One of you knows yesterday, one knows today. That makes a sound path.

S01-07.title: Rescue the Hunter
S01-07.summary: The hunter whistles for help. Animals drawn by his cakes arrive first. He wants to save his expert reputation. You need to save the expert.
S01-07.objective: Enter task map 1-2 and defeat the animals at the story question mark to rescue the hunter
S01-07.result: The animals retreat. The hunter and his notebook are rescued, providing a reliable clue to the hidden-stream entrance.
lines: A short whistle sounds deep in the pines, followed by an even more urgent shout.
Over here! Twisted ankle! My lunch has invited half the mountain's stomachs!
You sent dinner invitations with your distress call?
Weasel, rooster, civet. A full table already. I'm about to be the table!
Brace yourself against a rock. Stop holding up the food and competing for height.
My notebook slid down to the water too. Save the man and the notes if you can. Cakes come last!
At least the priorities are right. Stay there. We'll take the firm path over.
Prepare before entering the mountain. Don't add another person in need of rescue.
after_battle_lines: The animals retreat into the pines. You brace your pole across the wet ground, retrieve the notebook, and help the hunter onto dry stone.
You fished out both my life and my notes today.
Don't mention the cakes. One of us has to learn a lesson, and it won't be the flour.
Excellent. Our expert has progressed from a firm opinion to firm footing.
I know the hidden-stream entrance. Once I catch my breath, I'll tell you what I'm sure of, and what I'm not.
hints: You must enter the task map to answer the hunter's plea.
Defeat the enemies at the story question mark in task map 1-2 to complete the rescue.
Enter task map 1-2 from this node, trigger the story battle, and win.

S01-08.title: Lessons from a Hunter
S01-08.summary: You expect a peerless fighting technique. The hunter first moves his dried meat farther away. Lesson one: don't hang what the enemy wants around your neck.
S01-08.objective: Learn the hunter's advice on reading enemies and preparing for danger
S01-08.result: You hear the hunter's survival and preparation advice. No purchase or item consumption is required.
lines: A debt is a debt. I know a mountain skill that really can save your life.
Let's hear it. Preferably not whistling.
The hunter unhooks the food from his chest and puts it on a rock behind him. Then he points to animal tracks and the downwind slope.
First, see what it's watching and which way it's about to move. Whatever you're holding, keep something in reserve.
So plain a lesson counts as a secret art?
I failed at the plain part earlier. That's why you had to do the spectacular part.
I already fought your tuition fee. I'm not paying twice today.
No charge. Staying alive long enough to use it is better thanks than telling me it sounded impressive.

S01-09.title: Zhou Guangzu by the Stream
S01-09.summary: Zhou Guangzu lectures on the flow of plants and water. The fox on his shoulder jumps down for a drink. A thirsty mouth finds the fresh watermarks first.
S01-09.objective: Ask Zhou Guangzu to distinguish plants and old and fresh watermarks
S01-09.result: Zhou Guangzu supplies corroborating evidence about the watermarks, improving your notes on the plants.
lines: Plants have their pulse, waterways their course. Distinguish old from new before discussing where they lead.
Before he finishes, the fox on his shoulder darts down his sleeve, flattens a damp tuft of grass, and drinks from the lower water.
Your assistant has already handed in its answer.
It dislikes showing its working.
Wet roots below, fresh grass pressed downstream. The old channel above is dry.
Precisely. A fox finding water doesn't excuse you from examining the evidence.
After drinking, the fox climbs under his broad hat. Zhou steadies the brim, restoring his sage-like bearing by half an inch.
Understood. You explain the principle; it demonstrates it. I'll credit both of you.

S01-10.title: Master Willow by the Stream
S01-10.summary: The old map turned one stream into two. Master Willow's explanation is simple: both villages named the river. The river itself never split up.
S01-10.objective: Verify the hidden stream's outlet and local old names
S01-10.result: You confirm that Hidden Water and Willow Bend are local names for the same watercourse, and add a note.
lines: The upper village calls it Hidden Water. The lower calls it Willow Bend. A copyist asked both, then dutifully drew two streams.
The river stayed together. Its paperwork split into two households.
Different names may have different origins. Our ancestors were not always without deeper meaning.
Master Willow bends a long willow branch over the two old labels on the map, then points to the same current flowing at your feet.
Ponder the deeper meaning if you like. First establish where the water comes from and where it goes.
Put the other name in a note and join the stream. For once, the loudest voice hasn't won the map.
I also contributed valid evidence today.
Then record it. And leave a thought for the next traveler heading to the Xiang River: rivers have many names, and people have many versions.
